event.summary: Removing the restart read-generation floor does not by itself lose the interrupted-session override
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e

## TLDR
Considered whether a listing started before Restart could retire its successful outcome too early and leave the user seeing an interrupted-session card for a running session.

## Details
The patch removes the ReadGate generation argument from retire_confirmed_restarts. Source checks: session_ops.rs:63-81 defines read_confirms_run as stale or non-Interrupted, and explains that the retained success affects only Interrupted. The exact source rationale is: "for an interrupted session it still says Interrupted, and for any other the outcome has nothing to stand in for." restarts_retired_by also excludes pending sessions (session_ops.rs:91-109). session_view.rs references relaunched only as an override of Interrupted; terminal-kind selection was removed by this same commit. The removed floor therefore no longer protects terminal-kind information, and an old Interrupted row cannot retire the status override. This narrow concern is source-refuted; no runtime execution occurred. Suggested bucket: other (not reported). Confidence: confirmed for this considered mechanism. proposed_drop: source refutation described above. possible_cover: none; coverage sources were not searched. Could-be-highest: no; the considered consequence concerns terminal presentation rather than loss of work. Caveat: this does not establish all restart races safe; remaining callers and the changed specification still require review.

event.summary: A delayed stale listing can erase a successful Restart before the new run is classified
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e

## TLDR
After restarting an interrupted session successfully, a delayed list response from its earlier disconnection can make a newly opened view offer Restart again instead of attaching to the running agent. It recovers when a later read reports the new run.

## Details
view.rs:1985 removes the read-generation argument to retire_confirmed_restarts, and view.rs:3417 records the successful outcome without fencing the list reads. session_ops.rs:79-80 returns true for every stale row, including stale Interrupted, and restarts_retired_by at :91-109 checks only that no operation is currently pending; it no longer excludes reads started before the successful Restart. ReadGate.accept_success in ops.rs:183-189 accepts such a delayed response if no newer response or fence has applied. The normal single-flight reader queues the explicit post-Restart refresh behind the old request (reader.rs module contract; view.rs:2478-2492 at the earlier reviewed revision uses the same reader). Thus an old stale response can commit after pending is released and clear restart_succeeded before the follow-up read.

The stale premise is shipped: aggregate.rs:357 derives staleness from its captured host snapshot, and aggregate.rs:547-580 snapshots host connection state before awaiting the cached slice. A snapshot from a temporary disconnect can therefore be delivered after reconnection and a successful Restart. This requires ordinary response delay/ordering, not an invented control or a reproduction. Restart records its Unknown reply before answering (sessions.rs:3451-3483), but session_cache.rs:143-148 preserves a cached Interrupted status until a supervisor listing classifies the new run. A view opened in this interval seeds relaunched=false from the erased outcome (session_view.rs:615-633), and terminal_absence at :3701-3705 shows the interrupted card on a fresh, still-Interrupted detail row. Fresh Interrupted rows cannot restore the lost success. The earlier revision avoided this specific retirement through generation > restart_listing_floor (parent session_ops.rs:102-116).

Contract: SPEC.md, Lifecycle operations, says "A view opened during Stop or Restart observes that operation’s completion, including the terminal refresh or reattachment it needs" (ASCII apostrophe in source), and SPEC_impl.md:1134-1143 retains the successful reply so a view opened before the listing catches up can use it. Preserve ordering for stale rows too, for example retain the generation floor or fence list reads at restart completion.

Suggested bucket: other. The established consequence is a transient incorrect unavailable/restart surface; no loss of user work or destructive route is established. Confidence: likely, with the explicit timing premise that a stale list response captured before reconnection arrives after Restart completes and before the fresh listing/detail classifies its new run. All checks were source/contract analysis; no behavior was observed during execution and no reproduction was written. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none; coverage sources were not searched. Could-be-highest: no established security or loss-of-work route. Caveats: the pending check protects responses delivered before completion, and a later non-Interrupted read heals this; this finding does not claim a permanent failure or that clicking Restart twice necessarily loses work.

event.summary: An old stale sidebar response can erase Restart success before the mounted view consumes it
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: f560058da19e02716e6f943883a9508b447aff4e

## TLDR
After a successful Restart of an interrupted session, its open view can keep showing the interrupted-session card until its next detail read succeeds, instead of attaching immediately. An earlier sidebar response can erase the successful completion before the view sees it.

## Details
Synthesis correction: my original sequence incorrectly implied that a fresh connected detail GET uses the helm cached Interrupted status. It does not. sessions.rs:3052-3091 and :3194-3231 use manager::drain_sessions on the connected supervisor; only the no-client branch at :3160-3192 uses cache. session_cache::merged_status is relevant to the sidebar only. The established narrower route requires no fresh detail to remain Interrupted: it uses the already-mounted views pre-Restart current signal while the next detail is still pending. Preserve the original consequence (temporary wrong interrupted card instead of terminal); do not infer a persistent failure from cache.

Complete shipped source sequence: (1) A sidebar list request captures host-disconnected state and Interrupted metadata. aggregate.rs:547 captures manager snapshots before awaited cached_slice at :580; row_of at :357 derives stale from that captured host state. (2) The host reconnects; this independently reading mounted view has a live, nonstale Interrupted detail and can admit Restart. current is initialized from its selected Session at session_view.rs:603-607 and thereafter updated by accepted detail at :1032. The sidebar reader remains independent (:913-920); later parent selection updates follow only title and request detail (:1250-1273), not wholesale status replacement. Thus the old sidebar response need not match the mounted current state. (3) Restart succeeds. list/view.rs:3416-3419 records success, requests a sidebar refresh and releases its pending claim. Restart does not fence listing_reads. The explicit refresh coalesces behind the already-running sidebar request (reader.rs request discipline and list/view.rs:2473-2474), so the old response can still be first to commit. (4) The delayed old response completes after pending release but before the Restart observer consumes success. ReadGate accepts a generation newer than applied (ops.rs:183-190), not newer than Restart. view.rs:1985 calls retirement; session_ops.rs:77-80 treats stale Interrupted as confirmation, and :215-226 clears restart_succeeded. The removed parent floor excluded this read. (5) The observer sees the changed durable restart_revision but false success (session_view.rs:549-564): it increments mount_generation without setting relaunched. That increment is real, but keep_terminal_surface at :3714-3722 returns false for current nonstale Interrupted with relaunched false, so no terminal island exists to remount. The ordinary lifecycle effect at :1470-1490 requests fresh detail. Detail spanning an operation boundary is rejected by its sampled lifecycle revision (:927-975); a genuinely post-completion live detail subsequently repairs current and mounts the surface. No claim is made that such a new detail remains cached Interrupted.

Pinned scheduling check, not execution evidence: Cargo.lock pins dioxus core/hooks/desktop 0.7.10. Installed primary dependency source use_effect.rs:15-47 queues effects and reads shared state when they run; virtual_dom.rs:507-537 drains ready tasks before effects, with scopes rerendered first; scheduler.rs:61-78 explicitly ranks effects last. desktop webview.rs:537-590 waits for mutation delivery before continuing virtual-DOM work. A delayed sidebar task therefore can become ready and clear success after the completion render but before its deferred observer; no shipped ordering guarantees observer-first. This is an admitted source-level interleaving, not an observed schedule or a claim that it occurs every Restart. It does not need multiple GUIs, a new post-completion input, a lost reply or a second fault.

Contracts checked in full relevant clauses: SPEC_impl.md:1134-1143 says completion reattaches and mounted views observe it; SPEC.md Lifecycle operations retains action outcomes across view changes. SPEC.md Errors and diagnostics and One GUI at a time do not waive this successful single-GUI completion route. The sub-second input allowance says an action may be carried out as delivered; the pointer/key race acceptance concerns focus/selection. Neither establishes acceptance of erasing the completion before a mounted observer uses it. A transient detail error can lengthen recovery but is not required by the finding.

Suggested fix: retain ordering against pre-Restart sidebar responses or keep successful-completion knowledge durable separately from the seed retired for new views. Suggested bucket: other, unchanged. Confidence: confirmed source/contract interleaving for the mounted-view route; never observed in execution. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: duplicate known claims g037/f3 and g089/l1 at this same revision; g037s cache/detail wording requires the correction above. g036/l1 at b3d6b3eff6b7508e0b1fb6ec5b5cde31d27ebabe instead uses an eligible post-floor listing and optional terminal-kind payload, so its precise trigger/earlier terminal-kind consequence differs. g088/l1 correctly refutes losing the generation increment but does not refute keep_terminal_surface refusing to mount when the successful flag is gone. Could-be-highest: no established security or work-loss route. Caveats: later live detail normally heals the view; no lasting outage, fresh-detail cache staleness, or destructive second-Restart consequence is asserted. No runtime tests or reproductions run. No remaining missing source premise for this narrower route; actual incidence is unmeasured.

## TLDR
Deleting the final two sessions can leave a permanent stays/count notice for an environment this same window already knows has been destroyed. The rows can be gone while the success band still says the container or sandbox stays.

## Details
The new publication and retirement paths are ordered independently. publish_environment_delete at view.rs:590-607 installs kept text and its tag without consulting the current HostsRead. The only reconcile_hosts caller is accepted hosts-read completion at :2473-2476. A successful read showing the host absent/deleting retires a tag that already exists, but kept_band_after_hosts_read(None, read) does nothing; it cannot fence a later count publication.

Concrete shipped sequence within one GUI: confirm Session-scope Delete for session A and for its remaining peer B. Different-session actions are supported while A is pending. On the helm, sessions/sandbox.rs:176-265 serializes them using environment_delete_turn and the provisioning lock. A first receives Deleted { remaining: 1 }, forgets its own row and returns that count (:250-257); its lock/turn are released on function return, not on client consumption of the HTTP body. B can then delete the last session and finish_seal_locked destroys the resource (:259-263). Delay only As HTTP response/body delivery to this window. B and the resulting fleet/host reads can complete first. A successful hosts read now omits that destroyed host and reconciles the then-empty count tag. When As earlier successful body is finally consumed, view.rs:3005-3010 publishes its old remaining=1 message unconditionally, despite the retained HostsRead already proving the host absent. B need not fail, and no multiple-GUI allowance is required.

Why it can stay: the A completion refreshes only request_listing, through delete_refresh (:2910 and :3120-3132); its host-side forget and events already happened before B ran. request_listing and request_hosts are separate owners (:2510-2513). Feed notices read both (:2567-2574), but in this interleaving all destruction notices and their host reads may already be consumed before the delayed A response arrives. Ordinary successful list commits never call reconcile_hosts; a rerender does not either. The only automatic timer requests hosts when fallback_polls_now is true (:2580-2606), and feed.rs:233-234 returns false under a healthy feed. Other host-read triggers are explicit host mutation/creation, not this session Delete. Notice markup at view.rs:6110-6128 renders independently of remaining session rows. Hence no later host event/read is guaranteed to remove the new obsolete count in an otherwise idle healthy window. A dismissal, remount or unrelated later host read can repair it.

The new helper documentation and test (:6700-6785) explicitly require retiring a stays count after a successful current host read proves absent/deleting; that prerequisite has already occurred in this order, yet publication resurrects the count. event.summary: Existing notice publishers do not bypass the new kept-environment tag updates
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 2ef10815f12ed719ab6c51c6e3ac6fcd3f8bc1fa

## TLDR
Considered whether an existing caller could replace the visible Delete notice directly while leaving the newly added environment tag behind, allowing a later host read to erase an unrelated warning. The checked production publishers all use the shared methods, so that bypass route is refuted.

## Details
The new tag is the third field of DeleteNotice (view.rs:461-465). publish(Some) clears it after updating visible text; publish(None) preserves both; dismiss clears both; publish_environment_delete writes the text and tag returned by environment_band; reconcile_hosts clears them only when the helper returns a retirement (:580-620). A full pinned UI-source search for DeleteNotice/delete_notice found the production owner in lib.rs:2333, the export in list.rs:75, the ListView context and launcher context, and no direct production writer to delete_notice.0. The public signal field is read for rendering at view.rs:6110 and inspected by tests. Replace publication uses publish at view.rs:3348; both launcher result paths at create_form.rs:7089-7092 and :7148-7151 also call publish. Session Delete publication uses the scoped methods at view.rs:3005-3013. The existing setter regression test (:7368 onward) inspects publication ordering and same-display/None behavior, not a separate raw setter.

Suggested bucket: other for original suspected lost warning/presentation consequence. Confidence: confirmed source refutation of the checked bypass route, not execution. proposed_drop: no production raw-signal publisher exists in the pinned source, and the shared publication/dismissal methods update or preserve the tag with its text. possible_cover: none in supplied exact neighbour records; no prohibited coverage search. Could-be-highest: no established security or work-loss route; this considered mechanism concerns erroneous notice clearing, not remote deletion or lost files. Caveats: this does not refute l2s independent late-reply versus host-read ordering; all correct callers can still produce that race. It does not infer that the public field cannot be misused by future code. No runtime test, reproduction, build, live action or checkout modification. No unresolved premise for this candidate.
